contour.name: Budget, responsibility centre and funding
contour.scope: Versioned resource plan, scenarios, ceilings, allocations, funding sources and independent financial responsibility centres. Organizational structure and financial responsibility structure may differ.
questions: How are original budget, forecast, commitment and actual reconciled without conflation?
How is double counting prevented when multiple sources fund one project?
How does a cost/responsibility centre survive organizational reorganization?
invariants: Period, currency and accounting/recognition basis are explicit.
A plan or forecast revision never mutates actual transactions.
Every allocation has source, destination, basis, amount/weight and residual rule.
Historical postings retain the responsibility-centre version effective at posting time.
contour.acceptanceScenario: Two sources fund one project; then an organizational reorganization and budget revision occur. Original plan, forecast, allocations and actuals remain reconcilable without double counting or rewriting historical centre attribution.
contour.negativeCase: Moving a department rewrites past expenditure under a new centre or makes the same funding amount available twice.
contour.decision: Choose REUSE ONLY, PROFILE, or NEW MODEL. Determine whether WM-ECO-012 already owns scenarios and funding allocations, and whether a missing cross-domain Responsibility Centre master has independent identity/lifecycle. Do not turn organizational units or journal postings into that master.

catalogueSearchFinding: No dedicated Cost Centre / Responsibility Centre model or reserved registry entry was found. Multiple published models consume cost-centre codes, and WM-ORG-002 states finance is authoritative for cost centres while organizational-unit identifiers and ERP cost-centre codes are not the same identity.

model.name: Budget
model.purpose: Represent a governed, versioned resource plan and its authorization, allocation, execution bindings, forecasts and performance context independently of storage, exchange or user interface.
model.scope_statement: Owns budget identity, owner, boundary, period, basis, strategy, classifications, assumptions, scenarios, ceilings, funding, line estimates, proposals, review, authorization, allocations, availability, amendments, forecasts, variances, performance, controls, reports and standards projections while referencing actual transactions and neighboring master systems.
in_scope: Personal, project, organizational and public-sector budget profiles sharing a governed core
Objectives, programmes, estimates, classifications, ceilings, funding sources, proposals, authorization, allocation, availability, forecasts, amendments, variance, performance, risk and reports
Typed execution-system bindings, provenance, access, retention, audit, public transparency and standards crosswalks
out_of_scope: Ledger entry, transaction, commitment, obligation, contract, procurement, invoice, payment, revenue collection, cash account, asset, liability, debt or currency master lifecycles
Organization, person, programme, project, product, service, workforce, facility, classification, evidence, document and party master lifecycles
Universal tax, accounting, fiscal, appropriation, procurement, disclosure, cost-allocation or jurisdiction-specific authorization rules

boundary_notes.distinction: The budget owns plans, authority and mapped execution snapshots; the accounting system owns recognition, posting, adjustment, close and statements.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Transaction, Commitment, Contract, Procurement, Invoice and Payment
boundary_notes.distinction: These systems own legal and economic events; the budget stores typed references and reconciled amounts without becoming their master.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Revenue, Grant, Transfer, Debt, Asset and Liability
boundary_notes.distinction: Budget estimates and funding classifications reference external sources, positions and instruments, which retain their own identity and lifecycle.
The budget binds objectives, activities, owners, beneficiaries and indicators but does not own their structure, delivery events or evidence lifecycle.
Currency codes, exchange observations, classification code lists and calendars are external masters pinned by authority and version.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Policy, Law, Decision, Evidence and Publication
boundary_notes.distinction: Authorization, assumptions, decision records, evidence packages and released documents are referenced artifacts; none substitutes for the logical budget revision.

model.name: Organizational Unit
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to understand, create, inspect and operate the internal structure of an organization: which units exist, how they nest and report, what each is mandated to do, what establishment and staffing they carry, and how that structure is changed, dated, evidenced and disclosed over time.
model.scope_statement: This model covers an organizational unit as a subdivision that, in the words of the W3C Organization Ontology, 'only has full recognition within the context of that Organization'. It governs unit identity, classification, containment and reporting relationships, delegated mandate and decision rights, authorized establishment and measured staffing, structural change acts and their temporal validity, plus the provenance, retention, disclosure and interoperability rules that make the structure record operable. It deliberately stops at the boundaries of legal organizational identity, of the post/position as an object in its own right, of employment relationships, of physical sites, and of statistical or financial reporting units that are derived from - but not identical to - internal structure.
in_scope: Unit identity, naming, aliases and parent-scoped or ISO/IEC 6523 organization-part identification
Unit kind classification against governed code lists and unit existence status
Containment hierarchies, including multiple concurrent hierarchies (managerial, legal, cost, functional)
Reporting and coordination lines, including non-containment and dotted-line relationships
Delegated mandate, decision rights, authority limits and segregation-of-duties constraints attached to a unit
Authorized establishment (post complement) seated in a unit and its occupancy state at unit granularity
Dated headcount and full-time-equivalent measurement of a unit, with basis and aggregation thresholds
Reorganization acts (create, rename, reparent, merge, split, transfer, disband) and unit lineage
Effective dating, bitemporality and as-of reconstruction of the structure graph
Record authority, approval evidence, retention/disposition and disclosure control for structure data
Crosswalks to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, SCIM, schema.org and ISO/IEC 6523 projections
out_of_scope: Legal personality, incorporation, registration, LEI and regulatory identity of the whole organization (WM-ORG-001)
The post/position as an object with its own title, grade, job description and occupational classification (WM-ORG-004)
Employment contracts, appointments, persons and their occupancy of posts
Constitutive charter powers of the organization as a legal entity (charter model)
Physical premises, addresses, geometry and site operations (site/location model)
Statistical units such as enterprise, local unit and kind-of-activity unit used for economic observation
Financial segment reporting, general ledger and cost accounting mechanics
Stewardship policy machinery and access-grant issuance (S1/S2 service models)
Business capability, process and value-stream modelling
Identity-provider group membership and directory synchronisation state as a system of record

boundary_notes.distinction: W3C ORG separates org:FormalOrganization (recognized in a legal jurisdiction, with rights and responsibilities) from org:OrganizationalUnit, which has full recognition only inside its parent. Legal identity, registration and LEI stay in WM-ORG-001. A branch that is separately registered is dual-classified: it is a unit here and a legal entity there, and GLEIF only issues an LEI to the legally registered entity, not to an internal division.

org:Post represents a position that exists independently of who fills it. This model records only the unit-side facts: how many posts are established in the unit, which posts are seated there, and the aggregate occupancy state. Post title, grade, competency profile and occupational classification belong to WM-ORG-004, which this model CONTAINS by reference rather than by copy.

FHIR states that Location records where a service occurs while Organization records who performed it; Eurostat's 'local unit' is 'an enterprise or part thereof ... situated in a geographically identified place'. A unit may be associated with one or more sites, but premises, addresses and geometry are not unit attributes and are not modelled here.

Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/93 defines enterprise, kind-of-activity unit and local unit as observation units for economic statistics. These are derived by statistical rules from operational reality, not asserted by the organization, and their boundaries routinely differ from internal units. Treated as an ALIGN target, never as a source of internal unit identity.

IFRS 8 identifies operating segments through a management approach based on how the chief operating decision maker reviews internal reports, and permits aggregation of segments with similar economic characteristics. A reportable segment is therefore a derived view over internal units, not a unit; this model supplies the inputs and the change signal, not the segment determination.

RFC 4519 defines 'ou' as a multi-valued name attribute and RFC 7643 defines SCIM 'department', 'division' and 'organization' as free-text names. These carry no identifier, no validity period and no hierarchy semantics, so directory content is a lossy projection of this model and never its system of record.

ROR states it 'is not focused on capturing all subdivisions of a given organization such as a university's schools or departments' because departments 'often emerge, close, combine, and change'. No general governed global identifier exists for internal units, so unit identity is parent-scoped by default.

selectedFindings.name: Unit Kind and Classification Scheme
selectedFindings.description: Units are typed against a governed code list (department, division, directorate, branch, committee, board, team, programme office, shared-service centre, cost centre). W3C ORG provides org:classification against a scheme; CPOV constrains purpose to COFOG codes for public organisations and adds a classification property; FHIR uses a CodeableConcept type. The scheme must be named, versioned and resolvable, and the same unit may carry codes from several schemes simultaneously.

dataElements.name: unitKind
dataElements.description: Coded kind of unit against a governed scheme.

dataElements.name: classificationScheme
dataElements.description: Identifier and version of the scheme from which each code is drawn.

dataElements.name: isAlsoFormalOrganization
dataElements.description: Whether this subdivision is separately recognized as a legal entity.

selectedFindings.name: Reporting Lines and Their Standards Basis
selectedFindings.description: Reporting lines are distinct from containment: a unit may sit under one parent but report functionally elsewhere (dotted line). W3C ORG's org:reportsTo is defined between Agents or Posts, not between organizational units, so unit-to-unit reporting is an extension of the standard and must be declared as such rather than claimed as conformant. SCIM offers only a single 'manager' reference at person level, which cannot carry line type or validity.

dataElements.name: reportingLine
dataElements.description: Directed reporting relation with type, subject kind, target and validity period.

dataElements.name: reportingLineType
dataElements.description: Coded type of the reporting relation.

dataElements.name: standardExtensionNote
dataElements.description: Declaration that unit-level reporting extends beyond the domain/range of org:reportsTo.

selectedFindings.name: As-Of Reconstruction and Versioning
selectedFindings.description: Consumers need the structure as it stood at a past instant, both as it actually was (world time) and as it was believed to be at the time (record time). IFRS 8's requirement to restate prior-period segment information after an internal reorganization, or otherwise disclose the change, makes exact historical reconstruction an external obligation rather than a convenience. Reconstruction outputs must be reproducible and identified.

dataElements.name: structureVersionId
dataElements.description: Identifier of a reproducible structure state.

dataElements.name: contentDigest
dataElements.description: Cryptographic digest over the canonical serialisation of the structure state.

dataElements.name: asOfParameters
dataElements.description: The world-time and record-time instants that parameterise a reconstruction.

selectedFindings.name: Record Authority and Source of Truth
selectedFindings.description: Unit structure has no external registrar: the parent organization is the sole authority, unlike legal identity where GLEIF and business registers verify against authoritative local sources. Different attributes may nonetheless have different masters - HR for establishment, finance for cost centres, governance secretariat for mandates - so authority is asserted per attribute group, with a declared conflict resolution order.

dataElements.name: masterSystemRef
dataElements.description: The authoritative system for a given attribute group of the unit.

dataElements.name: recordOwnerRole
dataElements.description: The role accountable for the correctness of the structure record.

dataElements.name: ingestionTimestamp
dataElements.description: When an externally sourced assertion was ingested, kept separate from its event time.

selectedFindings.name: Evidence and Structural Validation
selectedFindings.description: A structural claim is only operable if it can be checked. Validation covers referential integrity against WM-ORG-001 and WM-ORG-004, acyclicity per hierarchy, temporal consistency, establishment-versus-actual variance, segregation rules and the FHIR-style minimum that an entry must have at least one name or identifier. Results are evidence, with severity and an owner, not silent failures.

dataElements.name: validationRule
dataElements.description: A named, expressible constraint over the structure graph with severity.

dataElements.name: validationResult
dataElements.description: Outcome of evaluating a rule against a unit or the graph, with instant and severity.

dataElements.name: evidenceRef
dataElements.description: Reference to a document or record substantiating an assertion.

functions.name: Resolve Unit Identity
functions.description: Resolve any inbound reference - master-system identifier, ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identifier, alias, former name, LDAP distinguished name or IdP group id - to the single current unit record or to a tombstone with a successor pointer.

functions.name: Validate Structure Graph
functions.description: Evaluate integrity rules over a structure version: acyclicity within each named hierarchy, single parent per hierarchy per validity interval, no orphans, referential integrity to WM-ORG-001 and WM-ORG-004, temporal gap and overlap rules, and segregation-of-duties constraints.

functions.name: Reconstruct Structure As Of
functions.description: Return the unit set, hierarchies, reporting lines and mandates valid at a given world-time instant as recorded at a given record-time instant, producing a deterministic, digest-identified view.

functions.name: Apply Reorganization Act
functions.description: Apply an evidenced structural change - establish, rename, reclassify, reparent, merge, split, transfer or disband - creating lineage edges, closing and opening validity intervals, and registering downstream obligations.

functions.name: Derive Org Chart Projection
functions.description: Generate a hierarchy view for a named hierarchy at an as-of instant, containing unit names and kinds only, with mandate detail and staffing deliberately excluded.

functions.name: Evaluate Mandate Conflict
functions.description: Detect overlapping or incompatible remits across units and breaches of authority limits or independence requirements, before or after a proposed structural change.

functions.name: Compute Headcount Rollup
functions.description: Aggregate staffing measurements up a named hierarchy under a declared counting basis and period convention, applying suppression where a cell falls below the minimum size.

functions.name: Reconcile External Directory
functions.description: Compare LDAP or SCIM representations of units against the governed structure, report drift, and push corrections outward without ever accepting the directory as a source of truth.

functions.name: Emit Standards Mapping
functions.description: Serialise the structure into a target vocabulary - W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR Organization, schema.org, or an ISO/IEC 6523 party identifier - using the versioned crosswalk and attaching a fidelity declaration.

functions.name: Apply Disposition
functions.description: Execute the approved retention schedule over structure records: destroy, transfer to archive or flag for review, while preserving the tombstones and lineage edges required for historical reference resolution.

functions.name: Assign mandate
functions.description: Attach or withdraw a remit, purpose code and delegation source on a unit for a validity interval.

functions.name: Seat post in unit
functions.description: Create or attach an established post in a unit independently of any holder. Occupancy is not performed here.

functions.name: Assert reporting line
functions.description: Record a supervisory or dotted-line reporting edge between units or posts with validity.

functions.name: Record staffing snapshot
functions.description: Store a dated established and filled count for a unit with basis and observation time. Treat as an extension until a primary unit-level metric standard is cited.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is outstanding for all sixteen base sources and for the two imported W3C ORG and CPOV anchors. Resolve the dated W3C ORG REC URI against the latest-version URI, confirm CPOV 2.1.2, schema.org v30.0 and the Peppol ICD list are still current, and pin FHIR deliberately, since the base cites R5 and the secondary provider cites R4.

ISO-derived structure is guidance-grade, not requirement-grade. ISO 37000:2021, ISO 30414:2018, ISO 15489-1:2016 and ISO/IEC 6523-1:2023 are paywalled and were reviewed only through committee decks, catalogue metadata and deployment profiles, so the delegated-authority, assurance and segregation findings must not be published as normatively sourced until clause text is verified.

ESRS S1-6 clause text was not machine-parsed; headcount, FTE, breakdown and the fifty-employee country threshold are stated at summary level and must be checked against Annex I of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 before any compliance-adjacent claim.

Unit-grain staffing measurement has no primary standard. Established-versus-filled counts, budgeted FTE and establishment complement are local controls; publish the measurement layer and record-staffing-snapshot as extension-grade with that limitation visible.

Multi-profile validation is incomplete. The model was tested chiefly against public-sector (CPOV/COFOG), healthcare (FHIR), EU reporting (IFRS 8, ESRS S1), directory (LDAP/SCIM) and e-invoicing (ISO/IEC 6523) profiles. Private-sector matrix organizations, military, academic-collegiate, ecclesiastical and cooperative unit forms are not validated and must not be presented as covered.

Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/93 was not retrieved from EUR-Lex; the statistical-unit boundary currently rests on a Eurostat glossary entry that cites it, and must be confirmed against the regulation text.

Regional scope must be stated on the face of any draft: CPOV, ESRS and the statistical-unit framework are EU instruments, NARA General Records Schedules bind US federal agencies only, financial alignment assumes IFRS rather than ASC 280, and employee consultation duties before a reorganization are jurisdiction-conditioned.

model.name: Position
model.purpose: Model the position as a durable, addressable organizational construct that exists independently of any occupant: the work assigned by competent authority, classified, placed, funded, requirement-bearing and lifecycle-governed, so agents can create, inspect, classify, staff and retire positions without conflating them with people, jobs or contracts.
model.scope_statement: In scope is everything that is true of a position while it is vacant. A position is the bundle of duties and responsibilities assigned by competent authority (5 CFR 511.101) and modelled as org:Post, which W3C defines as a position existing independently of the person or persons filling it. The model owns identity, titling, duty content, occupational and grade classification, structural placement and reporting, location and work arrangement, capacity (FTE/headcount) and funding, requirements and essential functions, delegated and prescribed authority, risk/screening designations, working conditions, lifecycle and effective-dated change, governance and evidence, and outbound interoperability. It does not own the person, the occupancy relationship, the employment contract, the recruiting workflow, or the taxonomies it aligns to.
in_scope: Position identity, keys, official and working titles, and language-tagged alternative labels
Assigned duties, responsibilities and essential functions attributed to the position rather than to an incumbent
Occupational classification, job/class membership, grade or level and job-evaluation outcome
Placement in an organizational unit, cost centre, reporting and supervisory structure
Work location, work arrangement and schedule attributes attached to the seat
Capacity and occupancy control: FTE, headcount, single vs pooled, overlap tolerance, vacancy state
Budget, funding source and the pay range or grade ladder framing the seat
Qualification, competency, credential, screening, clearance and approval requirements
Delegated decision rights and externally prescribed regulatory responsibilities allocated to the seat
Lifecycle states, effective-dated versioning, classification authority, certification, appeal and retention
out_of_scope: The natural person, worker or agent identity that may occupy the position
The occupancy relationship itself (appointment, assignment, tenure, occupancy dates) — owned by WM-ORG-016
The organizational unit as an entity, its charter and its own hierarchy — owned by WM-ORG-002
Team formation and team-level goals — owned by WM-ORG-003
Employment contract terms, payroll processing, absence and time records
Recruiting workflow: requisition approval chain, candidate pipeline, interview and selection records
The occupation, skill and competency taxonomies themselves (ISCO-08, ESCO, O*NET-SOC, NICE) — referenced, not owned
Individual performance appraisal, development plans and remuneration paid to an incumbent
Compensation plan and pay-structure master data (grade ladders and steps are referenced by key)

boundary_notes.distinction: The position persists while vacant; the assignment exists only while an agent occupies it. W3C separates org:Post (independent of holder) from org:Membership, which exists only when an agent occupies a role. Occupancy dates, tenure and incumbent-specific terms belong to the assignment, not the position.

A unit is a collection of people and functions with its own recognition inside a larger organization; a position is a single seat that is contained in exactly one unit at a time via org:postIn / org:hasPost. Unit charter, mandate and unit hierarchy stay with WM-ORG-002.

A position is an instance; a class is 'all positions which are sufficiently similar as to kind of work, level of difficulty and responsibility, and qualification requirements' (5 CFR 511.101), and an occupation is 'a set of jobs whose main tasks and duties are characterised by a high degree of similarity' (ISCO-08). Classifier definitions, code lists and hierarchies are external registries; the position holds only the coded reference and the evaluation evidence.

A vacancy notice is a published recruiting artifact with its own validity window, datePosted, validThrough and application channel; it is a projection referencing zero, one or many positions. HR Open keeps PositionOpening in the recruiting domain and organizational structure with incumbents in OrganizationChart.

W3C org:Role denotes the abstract role and requires a Membership instance to link a person, whereas org:Post is a concrete organizational seat. Role vocabularies (NICE work roles, ESCO occupations) are alignments, not the position itself.

Pay range, grade ladder and budget frame the seat; actual remuneration, contractual clauses and payroll results attach to the occupant's employment relation. EU pay-transparency duties bind the employer's disclosure at recruitment and reporting, not the position record's internal semantics.

selectedFindings.name: Unit and cost centre placement
selectedFindings.description: The single organizational unit that holds the position, the legal entity and business unit context, and the cost centre that carries it financially.

dataElements.name: Holding organizational unit reference
dataElements.description: The unit in which the post exists, corresponding to org:postIn / org:hasPost; mandatory department reference in production systems.

dataElements.name: Business unit reference
dataElements.description: Mandatory business-unit scope that also bounds position-code uniqueness.

dataElements.name: Cost centre code
dataElements.description: Financial owner of the seat, distinct from the organizational holder.

dataElements.name: Placement validity window
dataElements.description: Effective start and end dates for the placement of the position in this unit.

selectedFindings.name: Budget and funding source
selectedFindings.description: Whether the position is budgeted, what amount and currency it carries, and which funding source or existing position finances it.

dataElements.name: Budgeted indicator
dataElements.description: Whether the seat is included in the approved establishment budget.

dataElements.name: Budget amount and currency
dataElements.description: Monetary allocation attached to the position with an explicit currency code.

dataElements.name: Funding source reference
dataElements.description: Reference to the grant, cost centre or existing position that finances the seat, including the funded-by-existing-position case.

dataElements.name: Funding validity window
dataElements.description: Dates over which funding is committed, distinct from the position's own effective window.

functions.name: Establish position
functions.description: Create a new seat by recording the duties assigned by competent authority, mint its identifier and place it in a unit.

functions.name: Classify position
functions.description: Analyse the assigned duties and place the position in an internal class and one or more external occupational codes.

functions.name: Evaluate and level position
functions.description: Apply objective, gender-neutral evaluation criteria to assign a grade and allocate the position to a category of workers.

functions.name: Set capacity and funding
functions.description: Authorize FTE, headcount, position type and overlap tolerance, and bind the seat to a budget and funding source.

functions.name: Specify requirements and essential functions
functions.description: Record essential and marginal functions, competencies, credentials and experience required of any holder, using versioned catalogue references.

functions.name: Allocate authority and prescribed responsibilities
functions.description: Confer decision rights on the seat and allocate any regulator-prescribed responsibilities to it without leaving gaps.

functions.name: Designate risk and screening requirements
functions.description: Determine the clearance, vetting, regulatory approval and access requirements that attach to the seat before recruitment starts.

functions.name: Reconcile occupancy and vacancy
functions.description: Compute consumed and open capacity from assignment records and validate incoming occupancy against the authorization.

functions.name: Amend or reclassify position
functions.description: Apply an effective-dated change to duties, placement, capacity or classification, distinguishing correction from substantive change.

functions.name: Certify description and process appeals
functions.description: Certify the accuracy of the position description and administer challenges to its classification, applying decision effective dates.

functions.name: Publish position projection
functions.description: Generate an outbound projection of the position for a named recipient profile, applying suppression rules and disclosure duties.

functions.name: Freeze, abolish or dispose position
functions.description: Move the seat to frozen or abolished status and, at the end of retention, apply the governed disposition action to its records.

functions.name: Authorize fill or freeze
functions.description: Permit or withhold recruitment against a vacant Position, producing a fill-authorization that a JobPosting or requisition may reference.

publicationHolds: Source verification is incomplete: every base URL and version pin must be re-resolved at publication time. In particular the base cites 5 CFR and 29 CFR from the Cornell LII reproduction because eCFR and opm.gov were unreachable in its run, while grok reached eCFR current as of 2026-08-20 and the OPM classification standards PDF; re-verify and dual-cite or swap to the official host before publishing.

Source identifiers collide across providers with different underlying documents (SRC-002 is HR Open in the base and Popolo in grok, among others). All sources must be re-keyed during merge and every accepted addition re-pointed, and the merged source list re-verified as live, before any draft is published.

ISO 30400:2022 must not be cited as defining position, job, role or FTE: grok's own note concedes the term text was not inspectable behind the paywall, so only the standard's existence, date and scope are supportable. The ISCO-08 citation must likewise resolve to an authoritative ILO or UNSD host rather than the third-party netlify mirror used by grok.

Retention and disposition periods remain a declared gap. No fetched primary source in either pack states a retention period for position records, descriptions or classification decisions; the structure may be published only as a required local determination, never as canonical guidance.

Multi-profile domain validation is outstanding. Evidence concentrates on US federal General Schedule classification, UK FCA prescribed responsibilities, EU pay transparency and a single HCM vendor API. Before publication the model must be exercised against at least a civic or legislative profile (Popolo post with constituency), a healthcare profile (FHIR PractitionerRole unnamed slot) and a non-US private-sector profile, and every regional assumption must be labelled a jurisdiction profile rather than a universal requirement.

Published boundary notes must carry grok's disambiguations verbatim in substance: HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole is aligned, not equated, to a classified position, and the financial, geospatial and sports senses of the word position are excluded, including schema.org's Quarterback example of a named position.

model.name: Financial Transaction / Journal Entry
model.purpose: Model the atomic accounting posting: a balanced set of debit and credit lines recording one economic event in a ledger, with the identity, time, provenance, authority, evidence and retention context an agent needs to create, validate, post, correct, audit and export it.
model.scope_statement: The subject is one journal entry (posting document) treated as an aggregate: an entry header plus two or more posting lines that must balance, together with everything required to establish that the posting is authentic, authorised, correctly timed, correctly measured, and reproducible for audit. It covers the entry as recorded in a ledger of record and as exported for audit or tax inspection. It does not cover the accounts it posts to, the payment or invoice that caused it, or the financial statements derived from it; those are neighbouring models. The model is storage-neutral: SAF-T XML, XBRL GL instances, pipe-delimited audit data files, ERP tables, MongoDB documents and append-only ledgers are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Entry header and posting lines, their identifiers, and the balancing invariant between debits and credits
Monetary measurement: amount, direction, transaction currency, functional and reporting currency translation, rounding
Distinct time roles: document date, accounting effective date, posting date, value date, system entry (ingestion) time, approval time
Entry lifecycle from draft through posting to immutability, plus reversal, storno and correction linkage
Provenance: source system, source document reference, derivation rule, preparer, approver, batch and interface lineage
Authority and segregation of duties governing who may post what, where and when
Fiscal period assignment, period state (open, soft-closed, hard-closed) and cut-off treatment
Tax and analytical attributes carried on lines (tax code, taxable base, cost centre, project, segment, counterparty)
Validation, reconciliation to account balances, completeness of the extracted population and control totals
Audit risk signals on entries, supporting evidence, change-history and integrity controls
Access control, regulator and auditor access, retention, legal hold and lawful disposal
Export and exchange profiles (SAF-T, XBRL GL, audit data standards, statement entries) and code-list mapping
out_of_scope: Chart of accounts, account master data and derived account balances (owned by WM-ECO-015 Financial Account)
Payment initiation, clearing and settlement mechanics of a payment instruction (owned by WM-ECO-009 Payment)
Invoice and other commercial source-document content and their legal validity requirements
Financial statements, consolidation output and disclosure taxonomies
Legal entity, customer and supplier master records, including LEI issuance and KYC
Currency, unit-of-measure and country code registries as registries
Budgeting, commitment and encumbrance accounting, and management forecasts
Tax return computation and filing obligations
Consensus, cryptographic and network mechanics of distributed-ledger platforms

boundary_notes.distinction: The account owns the chart-of-accounts record and derived balances; this model owns the posting event and its balancing invariant. Account existence and status are referenced preconditions, never redefined here. Audit data and SAF-T structures likewise separate the chart of accounts and trial balance from general-ledger entries.

A payment is an instruction and a value transfer; a journal entry is its accounting representation. One payment may produce several postings in several ledgers, and a bank statement entry is the account servicer's own posting, not the customer's journal entry. Booking status and settlement finality are read from the payment side and only referenced here.

SAF-T and comparable audit files place source documents in a separate section from general-ledger entries. The entry carries a resolvable reference and a document archive number, but the legal content and format of the invoice belong to the source-document model.

Aggregation into statements, and the taxonomies used to report them, sit outside. XBRL GL provides an explicit mapping module (SRCD) to financial reporting taxonomies precisely because the two layers are distinct.
Counterparties are referenced by governed identifiers such as the ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier; the entry never becomes the master record for entity reference data or ownership structure.

REA models resources, economic events and agents at business level. This model deliberately covers only the accounting artifact derived from such events; duplicating resource and agent modelling here would collide with that ontology. The alignment is asserted at catalogue level only and is marked as an evidence gap.

selectedFindings.name: Journal assignment and entry typing
selectedFindings.description: Which journal or daybook the entry belongs to and how its nature and origin are coded.

dataElements.name: Journal identifier
dataElements.description: Code of the journal, daybook or subledger holding the entry.

dataElements.name: Entry origin category
dataElements.description: Whether the entry is manual, interfaced, recurring, adjusting, closing, reversing or consolidating.

dataElements.name: Bank transaction code
dataElements.description: Account-servicer classification of a transfer-derived entry (domain, family, sub-family).

selectedFindings.name: Ledger, entity and accounting framework context
selectedFindings.description: Which book the entry lives in, which legal entity owns it, and under which framework and functional currency it is measured.

dataElements.name: Ledger identifier
dataElements.description: Identifier of the book of account in which the entry is recorded.

dataElements.name: Reporting entity reference
dataElements.description: Governed identifier of the legal entity owning the ledger.

dataElements.name: Functional currency
dataElements.description: Currency in which the ledger measures results.

selectedFindings.name: Amount, direction and currency of a posting
selectedFindings.description: How a line's value and its debit or credit sense are represented, with scale, rounding and edge cases.

dataElements.name: Line amount
dataElements.description: Non-negative magnitude of the posting in the transaction currency, stored as an exact decimal.

dataElements.name: Credit/debit indicator
dataElements.description: Explicit direction of the posting, corresponding to debitCreditCode or CRDT/DBIT.

dataElements.name: Transaction currency
dataElements.description: Currency in which the line amount is denominated.

selectedFindings.name: Multi-currency translation and rate provenance
selectedFindings.description: Additional currency amounts stored on a line, the rate used, and how later revaluations link back.

dataElements.name: Reporting currency amount
dataElements.description: Translated amount in the functional or group reporting currency, with its currency role.

dataElements.name: Exchange rate applied
dataElements.description: Rate value, rate type and rate date used to translate the line amount.

dataElements.name: Exchange rate source
dataElements.description: Publisher of the applied rate, such as a central bank or contractual rate provider.

selectedFindings.name: Reversals, corrections and period-end adjustments
selectedFindings.description: Rare but required cases include auto-reversing accruals, prior-period corrections, consolidating and reclassification adjustments, late or unusual entries, and top-side adjustments that may not appear as formal journal entries in the general ledger.

dataElements.name: Adjustment class
dataElements.description: Reversal, correction, auto-reversing accrual, restatement, consolidation, reclassification or top-side.

dataElements.name: Original entry identifier
dataElements.description: Reference to the entry being reversed or corrected.

dataElements.name: Top-side flag
dataElements.description: Whether the adjustment is outside formal general-ledger journal entries.

dataElements.name: Post-close flag
dataElements.description: Whether the entry was recorded after books were closed.

selectedFindings.name: Initiate, authorize, record and process
selectedFindings.description: Controls must cover initiation, authorization, recording and processing of both automated and manual journal entries in the general ledger, subsidiary ledgers and other IT systems. Segregation of duties and dual control are expected except where a documented compensating control exists.

dataElements.name: Initiator identifier
dataElements.description: Person or system that initiated the entry.

dataElements.name: Authorizer identifier
dataElements.description: Person or system that authorized posting.

dataElements.name: Segregation of duties satisfied
dataElements.description: Whether initiator and authorizer are distinct as required.

dataElements.name: Control override flag
dataElements.description: Whether a control was overridden for this entry.

selectedFindings.name: Journal entry risk indicators
selectedFindings.description: The account, actor, timing and narrative characteristics used to select entries for fraud-focused testing.

dataElements.name: Risk indicator flag
dataElements.description: Named risk characteristic detected on an entry, with the rule that raised it.

dataElements.name: Risk score
dataElements.description: Composite score assigned to an entry by the selection routine.

functions.name: Draft a posting
functions.description: Create an unposted entry with header context and candidate lines, derived from a source event or entered manually.

functions.name: Validate an entry
functions.description: Apply structural, referential, balancing and business rules to an entry and report severities.

functions.name: Post an entry to the ledger
functions.description: Commit a validated, authorised entry to the ledger of record and make it immutable.

functions.name: Reverse or correct a posted entry
functions.description: Create a linked reversing or replacement entry rather than altering the original record.

functions.name: Translate a posting to reporting currencies
functions.description: Derive functional or group reporting amounts for a line from a governed exchange rate.

functions.name: Attach supporting evidence
functions.description: Bind a supporting document to an entry with a digest and custody metadata.

functions.name: Reconcile postings to balances
functions.description: Verify that posting movements explain the change in account balances for a scope and period, and analyse sequence integrity.

functions.name: Screen entries for risk indicators
functions.description: Score a population of entries against fraud-risk characteristics and select entries for testing.

functions.name: Close an accounting period
functions.description: Transition a fiscal period to a closed state and record the closing balances and residual items.

functions.name: Export an audit or tax file
functions.description: Produce a profile-conformant export of a declared entry population with control totals and mapping applied.

functions.name: Grant scoped auditor or authority access
functions.description: Provision time-bounded, scope-limited read or export access for an auditor, tax authority or regulator.

functions.name: Apply or release a legal hold
functions.description: Suspend or resume disposal for a defined population of entries and their evidence.

functions.name: Authorize journal entry
functions.description: Record the authorizer distinct from the initiator and attach the authorization event required before posting.

functions.name: Reject or exception-post to closed period
functions.description: Block posting to a closed period unless a documented exception grant exists for adjusting entries.

functions.name: Classify and reconcile a bank-booked entry
functions.description: Apply an ISO 20022 bank transaction code to a servicer-booked cash entry so it can be routed to the correct sub-ledger counterpart journal.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is outstanding: every accepted URL must be re-fetched and version-pinned, and the four base sources readable only at catalogue or metadata level (ISO 21378:2019 and ISO/IEC 15944-4:2015 paywalled; OECD SAF-T v2.0 guidance and the CPMI-IOSCO PFMI retrieved as non-extractable PDFs) must be labelled catalogue-level-only in the published draft, with no field-level claim resting on them.

Multi-profile domain validation is outstanding: the merged structure has not been exercised against at least two national tax-audit file profiles, one ERP journal projection and one ISO 20022 camt statement projection, so profile-specific field loss, code-list conflicts and round-trip behaviour remain unmeasured.

The privacy dimension is a declared gap in both providers: no data protection instrument was read as a primary source, so the personal-data and erasure-versus-retention treatment is structural only and must not be published as legal guidance.

No conformance claim to XBRL GL, SAF-T, ISO 20022, ISO 4217, ISO 21378, ISO/IEC 15944-4, IFRS or PCAOB standards may appear in the published draft; all external standards are recorded as alignments with their conflicts listed.

The entry-kind adjudication must be published with its rationale, including the fact that the two providers disagreed, so downstream Dimensions do not silently re-model the posting as a flat event record and lose the balancing consistency boundary.

Retention durations in the base are illustrated from a US securities rule and UK company law only; the draft must state that no universal period exists and that a per-jurisdiction declaration is required before any operational use.

model.name: Currency / Monetary Value
model.purpose: Provide an embeddable declaration of a monetary value on a host object: an exact decimal amount bound inseparably to an identified currency, with declared precision and rounding intent, an optional valuation date and conversion reference, and explicit value states, so that an agent can read, validate and reproduce monetary context without inferring any of it.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-032 is a mixin that a host object embeds when it needs to state a monetary value. Its boundary covers four concerns. (a) Currency identity: the code used, the authoritative catalogue and published edition it was resolved against, the code's class and status, and references to successor or redenominated codes. (b) Exact amount representation: sign, integer coefficient and decimal scale, canonical lexical form versus display form, zero and negative-zero handling, monetary intervals, and explicit exact, approximate, unknown, missing and not-applicable states. (c) Precision and valuation: the declared scale and rounding intent, the valuation date, and the reference to any conversion applied to reach the stated amount. (d) Governance of the mixin itself: ownership, catalogue pinning and integrity, supersession, and tombstoning of declarations. The model is never a currency master, a price, an account, a ledger entry, a payment, a transaction, a financial instrument or an economic event; it is the monetary field on someone else's object.
in_scope: Inseparable pairing of an exact amount with an identified currency reference on a host object
Currency code identity by alphabetic and numeric catalogue codes, with the catalogue and its published edition recorded
Code class and status as published by the catalogue: active, historic, registered fund, testing, precious metal and no-currency codes
References to successor or redenominated currency codes and to the catalogue amendment that recorded them
Exact decimal amount as sign, integer coefficient and scale, with canonical lexical form distinguished from display form
Declared scale, declared rounding intent and the digit bounds a host or profile imposes
Valuation date and the reference to any conversion applied, expressed as parameters of this declaration
Explicit value determinacy states and monetary interval endpoints, including explicit absence that is never expressed as zero
Governance of the mixin: catalogue pinning, integrity verification, supersession and tombstoning of the declaration
out_of_scope: Allocation, amendment, withdrawal or reinstatement of currency codes, which belong to the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency
Publication, amendment and supersession of exchange-rate series by a treasury, central bank or market data publisher
Country, jurisdiction, legal-tender status, exchangeability, capital controls or purchasing power, none of which are derivable from a currency code
Locale formatting: symbols, decimal separators, grouping, cash rounding increments and localized currency names
Prices, quotes, fees, invoices, accounts, balances, ledger entries, journal postings, payments and settlement
Financial instruments, cash-flow schedules, valuation methodologies and accounting or tax treatment
Arithmetic execution, exception signalling and rounding-mode implementation by a numeric runtime
Enforcement of policy, runtime evaluation of rules and the storage or evaluation of audit trails
Digital-token or crypto-asset unit identity registers and community or complementary currency registers

boundary_notes.neighbor: ISO 4217 currency and funds code register (Maintenance Agency lists)
boundary_notes.distinction: The register owns allocation, amendment, withdrawal and the published minor-unit values; this mixin only carries a reference to a code plus the list and published edition it was resolved against, and re-states none of the register's lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Locale display and formatting data (Unicode CLDR)
boundary_notes.distinction: Symbols, localized names, grouping, decimal separators and cash rounding increments are presentation owned by locale data; this mixin holds them only as optional labels and never treats a symbol as an identifier.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Financial message and payment models (ISO 20022 amount and currency types)
boundary_notes.distinction: Message profiles constrain amount digits and currency attributes for a payment instruction; this mixin defines the monetary declaration itself and owns no message, instruction or settlement lifecycle.

The publisher owns rate identity, effective periods, amendment and supersession; this mixin carries the valuation date and a reference to the rate used, and may derive a documented direct, inverse or cross-rate for a monetary calculation without becoming the publication authority for any source rate.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host object that declares the money (price, fee, balance, budget line)
boundary_notes.distinction: The host owns record identity, record lifecycle and the business meaning of the amount, including what a negative amount signifies; this mixin owns only the shape and integrity of the monetary declaration it contributes.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Numeric arithmetic environment (IEEE 754 decimal formats, general decimal arithmetic)
boundary_notes.distinction: The arithmetic environment owns operations, rounding-mode execution and exception signalling; this mixin only fixes the abstract number model used to represent the declared amount exactly.

selectedFindings.name: Authoritative currency catalogue and pinned edition
selectedFindings.description: A currency code only identifies a currency relative to a named catalogue, a specific list within it and a published edition. The ISO 4217 lists carry an explicit published-edition attribute and are amended over time, so a declaration must record which catalogue, which list and which edition it was resolved against, and must be able to verify the retained snapshot before resolving anything against it.

dataElements.name: Currency catalogue identifier
dataElements.description: Identifier of the catalogue or register that governs the currency code, for example the ISO 4217 code register maintained by its Maintenance Agency.

dataElements.name: Catalogue published edition
dataElements.description: The publisher's own edition marker for the list used, such as the published date attribute carried on the ISO 4217 lists. Retained exactly as published, never re-derived.

dataElements.name: Catalogue list designator
dataElements.description: Which list within the catalogue supplied the entry: current currencies and funds, registered fund codes, or historic currencies and funds.

dataElements.name: Catalogue snapshot digest
dataElements.description: Content digest of the retained catalogue snapshot together with the algorithm name, used to prove the snapshot resolved against was unaltered.

selectedFindings.name: Alphabetic and numeric code forms; symbols as labels only
selectedFindings.description: The catalogue publishes both an alphabetic code and a numeric code for an entry, and either may reach this declaration. Display symbols and localized currency names are ambiguous across currencies and must be carried, if at all, as presentation labels that never participate in identity or matching.

dataElements.name: Alphabetic currency code
dataElements.description: The catalogue's alphabetic code for the currency, carried as the primary identifying token of the currency reference.

dataElements.name: Numeric currency code
dataElements.description: The catalogue's numeric code for the same entry, carried when a host system exchanges numeric rather than alphabetic tokens.

dataElements.name: Currency display label
dataElements.description: An optional symbol or localized currency name shown to a person. Explicitly non-identifying, because the same symbol may denote several currencies.

dataElements.name: Display label locale
dataElements.description: The locale a display label belongs to, recorded so that a label is never reused outside the locale that produced it.

selectedFindings.name: Code class, status and published minor unit
selectedFindings.description: Catalogue entries are not homogeneous: alongside national currencies the register carries registered fund codes, precious-metal codes, a testing code and a code for transactions where no currency is involved, and it publishes minor units as not applicable for several of these. Class and status must be read from the pinned edition, and nothing about jurisdiction, legal tender or exchangeability may be inferred from the code.

dataElements.name: Currency code class
dataElements.description: The class the pinned catalogue assigns to the entry: national currency, registered fund code, precious metal, testing code, or no-currency code.

dataElements.name: Currency code status at pinned edition
dataElements.description: Whether the code was active or historic in the pinned catalogue edition, determined from the list that contained it rather than from current knowledge.

dataElements.name: Published minor unit
dataElements.description: The minor-unit value published by the catalogue for the entry, where one is published. Present only as a catalogue fact, not as the declaration's operative scale.

dataElements.name: Minor unit applicability flag
dataElements.description: Records that the catalogue publishes no applicable minor unit for this entry, which forces the host to declare an explicit scale rather than assume a default.

dataElements.name: Code resolution state
dataElements.description: Whether the code resolved against the pinned edition, and if not, the reason. Prevents an unresolved code from being treated as any currency.

selectedFindings.name: Successor and redenomination references
selectedFindings.description: When a currency is replaced or redenominated, the catalogue records the withdrawal and the successor arrangement. This declaration may carry a reference to the successor code and to the instrument or amendment that recorded it, so a reader can follow the chain, but it neither owns that transition nor re-expresses a historical amount in the successor currency.

dataElements.name: Successor currency reference
dataElements.description: A reference to the code that the catalogue records as succeeding a withdrawn code, carried as a pointer only.

dataElements.name: Published withdrawal period
dataElements.description: The withdrawal or changeover period exactly as published by the catalogue, which may be a month or a month range rather than an instant, retained verbatim without being widened into a false precise timestamp.

dataElements.name: Succession declaring authority reference
dataElements.description: Reference to the authority and instrument that declared the replacement or redenomination, recorded so that the chain is traceable outside this model.

selectedFindings.name: Amount and currency inseparability on the host object
selectedFindings.description: Amount, currency reference and declared scale form one indivisible declaration: published monetary datatypes bind them into a single type, and a value interchanged without a known currency code is not interpretable. The host object owns the business meaning, including what a negative amount signifies, and projections that split the parts into separate fields must still assert the binding.

dataElements.name: Monetary declaration identifier
dataElements.description: Identifier of the monetary declaration instance, assigned by the adopting Dimension only where the host cannot address the declaration through its own record identity and field path.

dataElements.name: Host object and field reference
dataElements.description: Reference to the host record and the field path at which this mixin is embedded, establishing who owns the business meaning of the value.

dataElements.name: Host-declared sign semantics
dataElements.description: What the host says a negative amount means in this field, for example a credit, refund or reduction. Declared, never inferred from the currency or from the model.

dataElements.name: Permitted sign set
dataElements.description: The signs the host field admits, used to reject a negative value where the host permits only non-negative amounts.

selectedFindings.name: Declared determinacy: exact point, interval, approximate or explicitly absent
selectedFindings.description: A monetary field must be able to say what kind of assertion it is making. Published monetary vocabularies support a value or a bounded range, and published absent-value vocabularies distinguish unknown, masked, not-applicable, unsupported and error. The declaration therefore carries an explicit determinacy state, so an absent or unknown value is never silently expressed as zero and an interval is never collapsed to a point.

dataElements.name: Value determinacy state
dataElements.description: The declared kind of monetary assertion: exact point value, interval, approximate value, or explicitly absent. Required so that no state is inferred from a numeric default.

dataElements.name: Absent-value reason
dataElements.description: When no amount is asserted, the reason for absence drawn from a declared vocabulary distinguishing unknown, masked, not applicable, unsupported and error.

dataElements.name: Interval lower endpoint
dataElements.description: The lower endpoint of a monetary interval, itself a complete monetary declaration carrying its own currency reference and scale.

dataElements.name: Interval upper endpoint
dataElements.description: The upper endpoint of a monetary interval, itself a complete monetary declaration carrying its own currency reference and scale.

dataElements.name: Endpoint inclusivity
dataElements.description: Whether each present interval endpoint is inclusive or exclusive, declared rather than assumed.

selectedFindings.name: Declared precision and scale versus observed digits
selectedFindings.description: A monetary amount carries a declared arithmetic context — scale, precision and accuracy mode — that is independent of the digits appearing in any serialisation. Trailing zeros, padded decimals and truncated text are representation artefacts; the declaration states which digits are meaningful and whether the value's exponent is preserved.

dataElements.name: Declared scale
dataElements.description: Number of fraction digits the amount is declared to carry, independent of serialisation.

dataElements.name: Declared precision
dataElements.description: Number of significant digits to which the amount is declared accurate, used where accuracy is expressed in significant figures rather than decimal places.

dataElements.name: Accuracy mode
dataElements.description: Which accuracy semantics the declaration uses: exact, accurate-to-decimals or accurate-to-significant-figures. The decimal-place and significant-figure forms are mutually exclusive.

dataElements.name: Exponent preservation flag
dataElements.description: Whether the original exponent within the value's cohort is retained rather than normalised, so that 1 and 1.00 remain distinguishable.

dataElements.name: Observed fraction digits
dataElements.description: Count of fraction digits actually present in the representation being inspected, recorded for comparison against the declared scale.

selectedFindings.name: Minor-unit metadata as a version-pinned currency property
selectedFindings.description: The number of minor-unit digits is a published property of the currency, not an implicit storage limit. It varies across zero, two, three and four digits and is absent for some funds, metals and index codes, and it changes when a currency is created, withdrawn or altered — so every use must pin the list or amendment version consulted.

dataElements.name: Currency code binding
dataElements.description: The alphabetic and numeric code identifying the currency or fund to which the amount belongs; the amount is meaningless without it.

dataElements.name: Minor-unit digits
dataElements.description: Published minor-unit exponent for the currency, such as 0, 2, 3 or 4; absent where the register records no applicable minor unit.

dataElements.name: Currency list version pin
dataElements.description: Identifier of the dated list or amendment from which the currency properties and minor unit were read.

dataElements.name: Profile maximum fraction digits
dataElements.description: Decimal limit imposed by the exchange or reporting profile in use, recorded separately from the currency minor unit because the two can disagree.

selectedFindings.name: Rounding mode, increment, direction and tie handling
selectedFindings.description: A quantization rule is interpretable only when mode, target exponent or increment, direction and tie handling are all stated. Accounting quantization to a currency minor unit, cash quantization to a non-decimal increment such as five cents, and custom contractual quantization are distinct named rules with different authorities and channel scopes — not variants of one default.

dataElements.name: Rounding mode
dataElements.description: Named rounding mode applied, drawn from the mandatory and optional decimal rounding modes rather than from a library default.

dataElements.name: Quantization increment
dataElements.description: Non-decimal increment to which the amount is quantized, expressed as an amount with a currency, for example a five-cent cash step.

dataElements.name: Target exponent
dataElements.description: Exponent the quantized result must carry when quantization is scale-based.

dataElements.name: Tie resolution rule
dataElements.description: How an exact half-way value is resolved, recorded explicitly because statutory and accounting defaults differ.

dataElements.name: Rule channel scope
dataElements.description: The channels and application points to which the rule applies and those it excludes.

selectedFindings.name: Exact, approximate and bounded monetary values
selectedFindings.description: Some amounts are exact, such as a stated payable sum; others are rounded, truncated, estimated or known only within bounds. The distinction must be declared, because comparison, aggregation and further rounding of an approximate value carry different guarantees, and the inexactness must be attributed to the operation that introduced it.

dataElements.name: Exactness status
dataElements.description: Whether the amount is exact, rounded, truncated, estimated or bounded.

dataElements.name: Value lower bound
dataElements.description: Lower bound of a bounded monetary value, expressed with the same currency binding as the value.

dataElements.name: Value upper bound
dataElements.description: Upper bound of a bounded monetary value, expressed with the same currency binding as the value.

dataElements.name: Inexactness signal raised
dataElements.description: Whether an inexact or rounded condition was raised by the operation that produced the amount.

functions.name: Parse and normalize an exact decimal amount
functions.description: Accepts an amount as a decimal lexical token or as an explicit coefficient-and-scale pair, and produces a normalized sign, coefficient and scale together with the canonical lexical form. Rejects any input that cannot be held exactly at the declared scale; it never rounds silently and never accepts a binary floating-point source as authoritative.

functions.name: Validate the currency reference against the pinned catalogue edition
functions.description: Resolves the declared currency code against the pinned, integrity-verified catalogue snapshot and reports the entry's class, status and published minor unit, or reports the code as unresolved. It reads the catalogue; it never allocates, amends or withdraws a code, and it never substitutes a default currency.

functions.name: Determine the declared value determinacy state
functions.description: Inspects a monetary declaration and reports whether it asserts an exact point value, an interval, an approximate value or an explicit absence with a reason, flagging contradictory combinations. Its purpose is to keep an absent or unknown value from collapsing into a numeric zero.

functions.name: Compare exact same-currency representations
functions.description: Compares two exact point declarations that resolve to the same currency code under the same catalogue, returning an ordering or equality result. Whether the two declarations are policy-compatible for comparison is supplied externally; the function neither judges compatibility nor converts between currencies.

functions.name: Validate a monetary precision and rounding policy declaration
functions.description: Checks that a declared precision and rounding policy is complete, internally consistent and resolvable: currency binding with a pinned list version, declared scale or increment, rounding mode, tie rule, precision tier and channel scope.

functions.name: Quantize an amount under an explicitly named rule
functions.description: Applies one named quantization rule — target exponent or non-decimal increment, mode, tie handling — to an amount and returns the quantized value together with every condition raised. No default rule is supplied: an unnamed rule is a failure, never a licence to assume two decimals or half-up.

functions.name: Expose the residual introduced by quantization
functions.description: Computes the signed difference between a pre-quantization value and its quantized result, or between two declared precision tiers, and returns it as a first-class amount so the host can disclose, carry or assign it.

functions.name: Allocate a total into quantized parts that reconcile exactly
functions.description: Distributes a total across parts under a named allocation rule with per-part quantization, assigns the residual to the target designated by the caller's rule, and returns a reconciliation difference that must be zero.

functions.name: Compare, order or aggregate values only under a compatible context
functions.description: Evaluates the compatibility predicate over currency binding, valuation basis and rounding context, and only then compares, orders or sums the values; otherwise it refuses with a typed incompatibility reason. It never converts, normalises or coerces implicitly.

functions.name: Bind valuation context to an amount
functions.description: Attaches a complete, versioned valuation frame — amount role, valuation instant and temporal kind, measurement basis with its defining authority, and market or scenario reference — to an amount that already exists in its owning record, without altering the amount value or currency.

functions.name: Select a declared rate under a caller-supplied policy
functions.description: Applies caller-supplied selection criteria — admissible sources, rate type, session, staleness tolerance and fallback order — to the candidate rate references resolvable in the owning publication model, and records which candidate was selected and why the others were not.

functions.name: Calculate a reproducible conversion
functions.description: Derives a converted amount from a preserved original using the selected rate or rate chain, applying a declared equation, chain ordering and rounding parameters, and emitting the full reproduction input set alongside the result.

functions.name: Reconcile original and reported values
functions.description: Recomputes a stored converted or reported amount from its retained reproduction inputs and compares the result with the stored value, classifying the outcome against the declared tolerance.

functions.name: Record a correction or supersession
functions.description: Issues a correcting valuation assertion that supersedes a prior one, capturing the reason, effective interval, issuer and approver, and emitting a serially numbered correction notice for the referenced notification and audit models.

functions.name: Check accountable role completeness
functions.description: Compare the declared role assignments for a monetary assertion against the role set required by its governing profile and report missing or expired assignments.

functions.name: Check segregation of duties declarations
functions.description: Test whether preparer, independent reviewer and approver references are distinct parties and, where they are not, whether a relief declaration with a compensating measure is present and unexpired.

functions.name: Resolve the effective monetary assertion
functions.description: Given a host reference, a role on host and a point in time, return the assertion version whose effective interval covers that point, together with its status and any superseding version.

functions.name: Check currency-list and policy pins
functions.description: Verify that the currency code-list pin and policy version pins are present and resolvable, and flag a code that has become historic or been replaced relative to the pinned list.

functions.name: Verify provenance chain completeness
functions.description: Check that a derived monetary value carries an original value reference, a derivation activity, an applied rate with its reference instant and retrieval time, and an attributed agent, and report which links are absent.

functions.name: Verify evidence integrity against manifest
functions.description: Recompute digests for referenced evidence items and compare them with the recorded integrity manifest, reporting mismatches, missing items and unrecorded additions.

functions.name: Derive published access attributes
functions.description: Compute the object attribute set and declared scopes that an external decision point consumes, from sensitivity class, restriction basis, handling labels and access exception declarations.

functions.name: Assess disposition readiness
functions.description: Determine whether the retention period computed from the trigger event has elapsed, whether any legal hold is active, and whether the host record's period is longer, and report an eligibility outcome.

functions.name: Report profile conformance and mapping loss
functions.description: Check mapping completeness against a named external representation and emit an alignment or conformance report listing mapped fields, unmapped fields and declared losses.

functions.name: Resolve effective monetary assertion version
functions.description: Select exactly one version of a bound monetary assertion for a stated effective instant and observation cut-off, and return it verbatim with a reproducible selection trace.

functions.name: Check binding and creation preconditions
functions.description: Evaluate every precondition for creating a monetary assertion and binding it to a host anchor, including currency-register validity, scale consistency, anchor resolvability and idempotency key state, and emit the precondition report.

functions.name: Plan a correction by supersession
functions.description: Compose a correction plan that names the version to be superseded and its validator, states the replacement values, closes the prior effective interval, and reports overlap and gap conditions across the version series.

functions.name: Compile review and approval evidence
functions.description: Assemble the evidence set for a proposed monetary state change, verify evidence validity intervals, status and securing proofs, and report completeness with named gaps.

functions.name: Report advisory eligibility for a monetary operation
functions.description: Assemble the subject, object, operation and environment attributes for a requested read or change and emit a non-binding eligibility statement that names the external component holding decision authority.

functions.name: Report disposition readiness
functions.description: Assess whether a monetary assertion is ready for removal by collecting holds in force, the referenced retention class, reference-integrity results and outstanding blockers, and emit the readiness report with proposed tombstone content.

functions.name: Describe an operation failure
functions.description: Render any refusal, precondition failure, conflict or unresolvable reference from the operations above as a machine-identifiable failure descriptor with a resolvable type and a stable title.

functions.name: Validate monetary value
functions.description: Evaluate a monetary value for admissibility against a caller-pinned profile and a referenced currency register version, returning typed outcomes without altering the value.

functions.name: Quantise amount
functions.description: Round an exact amount to a target scale under a referenced rounding policy and report the signed residual and the resulting value interval.

functions.name: Allocate quantisation residual
functions.description: Distribute the residual arising when a quantised total is split into components, so that the quantised components sum exactly to the quantised total.

functions.name: Value or convert monetary value
functions.description: Restate a monetary value in a target currency or under a target measurement basis using a rate binding supplied by the caller, emitting a complete derivation record.

functions.name: Reconcile monetary values
functions.description: Compare a set of monetary values against a stated total or against one another within a declared tolerance and report the verdict with attribution of any difference.

functions.name: Project monetary value to target representation
functions.description: Map a monetary value and its precision into a named target representation, declaring any scaling or rounding introduced by the projection.

functions.name: Apply authorised redaction to a monetary projection
functions.description: Apply an already-authorised disclosure-protection operation — suppression, banding, controlled rounding or interval publication — to a monetary projection and declare the resulting information loss.
